extracted.intended_audience: taxpayers (fuel industry) removing dyed fuel, tax practitioners, and members of the public submitting comments on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulations providing eligibility, reporting, recordkeeping, and claim procedures for payments under Internal Revenue Code section 6435 (payments for previously taxed dyed diesel fuel or kerosene), together with instructions for submitting public comments and requests for a hearing on the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6435 payment eligibility / claimant burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6435(a) requires that a person claiming a payment under section 6435 establish to the satisfaction of the Secretary of the Treasury or the Secretary's delegate that such person meets the requirements under section 6435(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6435 allows a person that establishes to the satisfaction of the Secretary that the person removed eligible indelibly dyed diesel fuel or kerosene (eligible dyed fuel) from a terminal to claim a payment (without interest) equal to the amount of the section 4081 tax previously paid with respect to such dyed fuel. The Treasury Department and the IRS lack authority to pay section 6435 claims to anyone other than the person that paid the section 4081 tax to the IRS with respect to the eligible dyed fuel to which the claim relates (see Announcement 2026-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of eligible claimant / affected taxpayers
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed regulations would affect taxpayers that withdraw previously taxed dyed fuel from a terminal; specifically taxpayers removing dyed fuel from an approved terminal with respect to which they previously paid tax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These taxpayers are a narrow subset of businesses within the fuel industry and a subset of taxpayers filing Form 720 for certain diesel fuel and kerosene taxes. The preamble notes that most identifiable filers are large, sophisticated businesses; no historical data for section 6435 claimants exists because the section first went into effect December 31, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability date
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §48.6435-1 would apply to removals of eligible dyed fuel occurring on or after December 31, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section 7805(b)(2). The temporary regulations add §48.6435-1T and the text of that temporary regulation is the same as the text of the proposed §48.6435-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reporting form and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed regulations set forth intended collections of information to be provided to the IRS with Form 8849, Claim for Refund of Excise Taxes, and Schedule 5 (Form 8849), Section 4081(e) and 6435 Claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The collections of information include reporting and recordkeeping necessary to ensure a taxpayer qualifies for a section 6435 refund. These forms and form instructions are already approved under OMB control number 1545-1420.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting content and filing procedures (including model report)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed regulations would establish reporting procedures, including a model report, that allow the IRS to verify a taxpayer's entitlement to a payment under section 6435 as contemplated by the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting requirements include execution and filing of reports as detailed in proposed §48.6435-1(e). The report is the mechanism to make a section 6435 claim; the preamble estimates fewer than 60 taxpayers will prepare one or more such reports annually and each report will take no more than one hour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping retention requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Books or records relating to a collection of information must be retained as long as their contents may become material in the administration of any Internal Revenue law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recordkeeping requirements would include that a taxpayer keep records to establish its eligibility for and the amount of a section 6435 claim. Tax returns and tax return information are generally confidential as required by 26 U.S.C. 6103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, an agency must obtain OMB approval before collecting information from the public; an agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a valid OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed regulations would not change or create new collection requirements beyond those already reviewed and approved by OMB under the temporary regulations. Forms cited (Form 8849 and Schedule 5) are approved under OMB control number 1545-1420.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and use of collected information
rubrics_metrics.description: The collections of information would be used by the IRS for tax compliance purposes and by taxpayers to establish eligibility for a section 6435 refund; generally tax returns and tax return information are confidential under 26 U.S.C. 6103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although information is generally confidential, the Treasury Department and the IRS will publish for public availability any comments submitted to the IRS's public docket on Regulations.gov. Agencies may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and address for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters are strongly encouraged to submit public comments electronically via the Federal eRulemaking Portal at https://www.regulations.gov (indicate IRS and REG-119294-25) by following the online instructions for submitting comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send paper submissions to: CC:PA:01:PR (REG-119294-25), Room 5503, Internal Revenue Service, P.O. Box 7604, Ben Franklin Station, Washington, DC 20044. A plain language summary of the proposed regulations will be available at Regulations.gov. Alternative ways to comment (Regulations.gov link) are noted. Once submitted to the Portal, comments cannot be edited or withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Written or electronic comments and requests for a public hearing must be received by June 30, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments are considered public and will be posted online once the Treasury Department has reviewed them. Any comments will be made available at https://www.regulations.gov or upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for a public hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A public hearing will be scheduled if requested in writing by any person that timely submits electronic or written comments; requests for a public hearing must be submitted as prescribed in the 'Comments and Requests for a Public Hearing' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a public hearing is scheduled, a notice of the date, time, and place for the public hearing will be published in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) certification and invitation for comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the RFA, it is certified that these proposed regulations will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities within the meaning of section 601(6) of the RFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Treasury Department and the IRS invite comments from any party, particularly affected small entities, on the accuracy of this certification. The notice also states submission to the Chief Counsel for the Office of Advocacy of the SBA for comment on impact on small business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 202 of UMRA requires agencies to assess anticipated costs and benefits for rules that may result in expenditures above a statutory threshold; these proposed regulations do not include any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures in excess of that threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble states the proposed regulations do not include such a federal mandate by the private sector or governments that would trigger the UMRA threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13132 prohibits an agency from publishing any rule that has federalism implications unless certain conditions are met; these proposed rules do not have federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble states the rules do not impose substantial direct compliance costs on State and local governments, nor preempt State law within the meaning of the Executive Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for the proposed regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed amendments to 26 CFR part 48 (including §48.6435-1) are proposed under the authority of sections 6435(a), 6001, and 7805(a) of the Internal Revenue Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority citation for part 48 is amended to add an entry for §48.6435-1. Section 6001 authorizes prescribing regulations related to recordkeeping, statements, and returns; section 7805(a) authorizes all needful rules and regulations for enforcement of the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary regulation text adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the proposed §48.6435-1 is the same as the text of §48.6435-1T in the temporary rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains that temporary regulations add §48.6435-1T and that the temporary regulations relate to statutory provision providing for payments; the text of the temporary regulations serves as the text of these proposed regulations.
